factors.name: Cash Conversion Forecast Veto
factors.description: Form an expectation impulse from changes in epsEstimate and revenueEstimate, then multiply it by a cash-validation score based on changes in cashConversionCycle, incomeQuality, receivablesGrowth, inventoryGrowth, and operatingCashFlowGrowth. Cross-sectionally rank the signed validated impulse within sector.
factors.trading_idea: Consensus upgrades can be low quality when reported growth is being financed through deteriorating working capital rather than cash generation. Long firms with improving revenue or EPS expectations that are corroborated by stable-to-improving cashConversionCycle, operatingCashFlowGrowth, and incomeQuality; short firms where favorable expectations conflict with receivables or inventory build and worsening cash conversion. The mispricing persists because headline estimate changes are highly salient while the working-capital details that challenge them are costly to parse and are updated only at reporting dates.

factors.name: Consensus Revision Absorption Deficit
factors.description: Detect point-in-time changes in epsEstimate and revenueEstimate, standardize each by its own trailing absolute-change scale, and subtract the contemporaneous short-window industry-relative return reaction. Combine positive revision minus muted reaction as a long score and negative revision minus muted reaction as a short score.
factors.trading_idea: Analyst consensus changes are sparse, salient fundamental-information events, but investors often anchor on the pre-revision price narrative and absorb the news gradually. The signal targets upgrades or downgrades for which the corresponding price response has been unusually small relative to industry peers, leaving an unassimilated information deficit. The hypothesis is falsified if price-insensitive revisions have no subsequent directional drift or if their predictive content disappears after normalizing by revision magnitude and volatility.

factors.name: Dual-Estimate Assimilation Slope
factors.description: At estimate-update dates, compute cross-sectional standardized changes in epsEstimate and revenueEstimate, combine them only when their signs agree, and subtract the recent sector-neutral return response. The signal favors large unassimilated, internally consistent revisions and is zeroed when neither estimate changes.
factors.trading_idea: Analysts often update EPS and revenue expectations together, but short-horizon prices can absorb only the headline component of the revision. Long firms with concordant positive EPS and revenue estimate innovations whose sector-neutral price response is still small, and short the converse. The hypothesis is falsified if fully reacted and under-reacted revisions have indistinguishable subsequent returns; the likely counterparty is investors reacting to the most salient estimate headline rather than the joint information set.

factors.name: Cash-Conversion Growth Quality Spread
factors.description: Form a quarterly innovation in operatingCashFlow divided by revenue, penalized by contemporaneous receivablesGrowth, inventoryGrowth, and changeInWorkingCapital scaled by revenue. Rank the resulting cash-backed growth measure cross-sectionally, optionally requiring positive revenueGrowth to distinguish improving collection from a shrinking business.
factors.trading_idea: Revenue growth is more likely to persist when cash conversion improves without an accompanying build in receivables, inventory, or working-capital needs. Investors frequently reward reported top-line growth before the next filing clarifies whether that growth was collected in cash, creating a cross-sectional quality spread. The mechanism fails if firms with improving operating-cash-flow-to-sales and benign working-capital changes do not subsequently outperform nominally similar growth firms.

factors.name: Accelerating Signed-Impact Elasticity
factors.description: Use close location within the daily range times volume as a signed-flow proxy, then compare short- and medium-window rolling return-on-signed-flow slopes. The factor favors stocks whose impact elasticity is accelerating in the direction of the recent signed-flow imbalance, with extreme one-bar gaps winsorized.
factors.trading_idea: Price pressure is more informative when each additional unit of signed volume proxy generates increasingly large price movement, because available liquidity is being depleted rather than replenished. A rising causal estimate of return sensitivity to close-location-signed volume should forecast short-run continuation while liquidity providers widen or withdraw and execution programs complete. The hypothesis is rejected if accelerated impact is followed by systematically lower, rather than higher, same-direction returns after controlling for the size of the initiating move.

factors.name: Downside Commonality and Balance-Sheet Convexity
factors.description: Estimate separate rolling correlations of each stock with its leave-one-out sector basket on positive and negative sector-return days, take the downside-minus-upside correlation spread, and interact it with debtToEquity, currentRatio, and interestCoverage ranks. The output is a cross-sectional fragility score rather than a raw volatility rank.
factors.trading_idea: Stocks whose correlation with their sector sharply rises only on sector down days have embedded downside common-shock exposure that conventional unconditional beta understates. High leverage, weak liquidity, or low interest-coverage firms should be especially vulnerable because a sector shock tightens both equity-risk limits and perceived financing capacity, creating forced-risk reduction beyond the initial move. Short the most downside-common, financially fragile names and buy low-commonality resilient names; the idea fails if conditional correlation asymmetry does not predict relative downside after controlling for ordinary volatility.

factors.name: Subcritical Marked-Shock Branching Headroom
factors.description: Define signed shock events from abnormal close-to-close returns jointly exceeding rolling volume and range thresholds. Estimate separate exponentially decayed positive and negative event intensities and a rolling branching proxy from lagged event-response slopes; rank the latest signed intensity only when branching is positive, elevated, and below a saturation cutoff.
factors.trading_idea: Directional abnormal-volume shocks often cluster because institutional execution, stop activation, and attention create self-exciting sequences rather than isolated observations. A fresh shock has continuation value when the estimated excitation process is active but still subcritical: there is evidence of a cascade, without the late-stage saturation that tends to exhaust liquidity and reverse. The mechanism is falsified if continuation is equally strong after estimated branching intensity is near or above one, where the proposed headroom distinction should matter.

factors.name: Industry Shock Convexity Receiver
factors.description: Estimate each stock's rolling response separately to modest and tail leave-one-out industry returns; use the difference as a tail-transmission loading. Multiply that loading by the current signed industry shock and subtract the stock's contemporaneous beta-predicted response, producing a signed catch-up score.
factors.trading_idea: Information and forced positioning propagate through economically linked firms with a delay, but the first movers in an industry are not necessarily the firms with the largest eventual exposure. A receiver with historically high convex sensitivity to large peer moves, but little reaction to the current leave-one-out industry impulse, is an underpriced contagion target. The trade is falsified if delayed receivers do not catch up after conditioning on their own beta, liquidity, and recent idiosyncratic news.

factors.name: Accounting State-Jump Attention Lag
factors.description: At each newly available fundamental update, construct a standardized state-change vector from operating cash flow, free cash flow, revenue, operating margin, receivables growth, inventory growth, debt growth, and net stock issuance. Score the magnitude and internal coherence of the update, signed by improvement versus deterioration, then retain observations where contemporaneous abnormal volume and price displacement are small relative to the fundamental jump.
factors.trading_idea: A quarterly disclosure can alter several economically linked accounting dimensions at once, but investors often process the headline EPS or revenue number before reconciling cash conversion, working-capital changes, and capital structure implications. The factor targets large, internally coherent fundamental-state jumps whose immediate price-and-volume response is muted, expecting delayed repricing as slower fundamental investors absorb the broader update. The hypothesis is falsified if coherent multi-field updates with initially weak market engagement do not generate systematically signed six-bar residual returns; the other side is attention-constrained traders and mandate-constrained investors who cannot fully re-underwrite each filing immediately.

factors.name: Systematic Risk-Mode Rotation
factors.description: Compute rolling daily-return correlation matrices across the universe, estimate the leading eigenvector each day, and measure each ticker's change in normalized leading-mode loading over a trailing interval. Cross-sectionally rank the signed loading change, optionally interacting it with recent return direction and realized range volatility.
factors.trading_idea: A rapid increase in a stock's loading on the dominant cross-sectional return-correlation mode identifies names becoming newly exposed to systematic de-risking before many volatility-targeting and index-oriented investors have fully resized. The signal is bearish for stocks with sharply rising common-mode loadings, especially when their recent return is already negative, and bullish for names whose common-mode exposure is falling. This mechanism should fail if changes in estimated eigenvector loading do not predict subsequent relative returns after controlling for realized volatility; the other side is slow-moving benchmarked capital that adjusts exposure using delayed covariance estimates.

factors.name: Liquidity Elasticity Curvature
factors.description: Estimate daily impact elasticity as intrabar range divided by dollar-volume proxy, using close times volume with robust floors. Measure the curvature of short-, medium-, and longer-window elasticity estimates, multiply by recent directional close location, and rank the resulting signed fragility score cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: A rising sequence of price-range-per-unit-volume readings indicates that progressively less trading is required to move the price, a daily-bar proxy for deteriorating liquidity depth. When this elasticity steepens in the direction of the recent signed close-location pressure, the market is more vulnerable to a continuation jump because marginal liquidity suppliers have withdrawn. The effect should disappear if future range and directional return are unrelated to elasticity curvature after conditioning on ordinary volume and volatility; the other side is liquidity providers and risk managers who reduce quoted risk only gradually.

factors.name: Catalyst-Conditioned Bar-State Compressibility
factors.description: Detects fresh changes in epsSurprise and revenueSurprise, signs them by the standardized surprise direction, and weights them by low rolling transition entropy of discretized daily return sign and relative-volume states. The output is cross-sectionally ranked within date, with stale or missing fundamental observations suppressed.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings or revenue surprise is more likely to continue when subsequent daily price-volume states become unusually predictable rather than noisy. This is a daily-bar analogue of the low-entropy informed-flow state in the source paper: persistent informed execution makes the sequence of signed returns and relative-volume states compressible, while the surprise supplies the direction that entropy alone cannot identify. The edge should disappear if low-compressibility names do not exhibit larger post-surprise drift than equally surprised but high-compressibility names; arbitrage is limited because the underlying event is sparse and execution urgency is not directly observable.

factors.name: Autocorrelation-Timed Conservative Tilt
factors.description: Construct a daily conservative score from low assetGrowth, low capexToOperatingCashFlow, low debtGrowth, and high freeCashFlowYield. Form the daily return spread between conservative and aggressive score buckets, estimate its smoothed lagged persistence, and multiply the stock-level conservative score by the signed, volatility-scaled expected spread.
factors.trading_idea: Rather than holding a permanent conservative-minus-aggressive exposure, condition the cross-sectional investment tilt on the recent persistence of its realized factor premium. The source paper argues that factor-premium autocorrelation can contain timing information; static smart-beta and benchmarked investors are the natural opposite side when they maintain exposure through adverse regimes. The mechanism is falsified if the lagged conservative-minus-aggressive premium does not improve prediction of the next six-day factor spread relative to an unconditional conservative tilt.

factors.name: Accrual-Valuation Momentum Disagreement
factors.description: Create an earnings-quality deterioration score from declining incomeQuality, operatingCashFlowGrowth below netIncomeGrowth, rising receivablesGrowth relative to revenueGrowth, and weak freeCashFlowGrowth. Interact this score with sector-relative valuation and recent price momentum, assigning negative scores to expensive price winners with worsening cash realization and positive scores to cheap price losers with improving realization.
factors.trading_idea: Price momentum is least credible when it asks investors to capitalize low-quality reported earnings that are not backed by operating cash flow. Growth and momentum mandates can continue rewarding the headline earnings path, whereas fundamental investors face reporting-frequency and short-sale constraints in arbitraging the divergence immediately. The hypothesis is falsified if positive momentum among firms with deteriorating incomeQuality, rising receivablesGrowth, and elevated valuation is no more likely to reverse than momentum among cash-confirmed firms.

factors.name: Valuation-Weighted Peer Momentum Extrapolation
factors.description: Combine a stock's peer-relative return over a medium rolling window with cross-sectional valuation duration proxies such as psRatio, evToSales, pegRatio, and pfcfRatio. Penalize positive extrapolative momentum when recent epsEstimate and revenueEstimate changes are weak, and symmetrically reward negative over-extrapolation among fundamentally supported firms.
factors.trading_idea: Investors extrapolate strong peer-group price action more aggressively into expensive, long-duration firms whose valuation already embeds ambitious growth assumptions. The proposed trade shorts high-valuation stocks whose recent peer-relative momentum is strong but unsupported by fresh estimate revisions, while buying cheap or financially resilient names facing the symmetric pessimistic extrapolation. A null result after conditioning on valuation and revision state would reject the behavioral mechanism; limits to arbitrage include shorting costs, career risk, and the difficulty of timing enthusiasm for growth narratives.

factors.name: Convex Growth Narrative Unwind
factors.description: Measure curvature of the recent log-price path using a causal quadratic fit, then interact positive curvature with negative changes in revenueGrowth, epsEstimate, operatingMargin, or grossMargin relative to industry peers. Assign the most negative scores to high-valuation names with the strongest price-fundamental acceleration mismatch.
factors.trading_idea: Momentum extrapolation is most fragile when a stock's price path becomes convex while the underlying growth narrative is flattening rather than accelerating. Investors can chase an easily visible breakout and anchor on stale high growth, whereas quarterly revenue growth, estimate revisions, and margin changes reveal that incremental delivery has weakened. The hypothesis is rejected if convex price acceleration paired with decelerating operating evidence continues to outperform over the next week; natural buyers are trend-following and benchmarked growth investors with limited ability to short expensive names.

factors.name: Downside Variance Scale Propagation
factors.description: Use causal rolling range-based variance estimates over short, medium, and slow windows, separately for negative-return and positive-return days. Score the signed change in the downside variance term structure: localized short-scale downside spikes are positive reversal candidates, while broadening downside variance across all scales is a negative continuation candidate.
factors.trading_idea: Crisis amplification is more dangerous when a volatility shock propagates from a short-lived range burst into medium- and long-memory variance components. A compact downside shock that remains localized at the shortest scale is often over-discounted and can rebound, whereas a downside shock whose variance is spreading coherently across scales reflects a broader deleveraging regime and should persist. This mechanism is rejected if cross-scale propagation does not distinguish future returns from total realized volatility alone.

factors.name: Crisis Semibeta Financing Wedge
factors.description: Use the equal-weight cross-sectional return as a market proxy and estimate each stock's rolling beta only on negative-market days. Combine the semibeta with sector-relative ranks of cashRatio, debtToEquity, interestCoverage, and operatingCashFlow relative to totalDebt, with the strongest score assigned to fragile high-downside-beta names.
factors.trading_idea: During market-down days, investors and lenders care disproportionately about downside beta rather than unconditional beta. Firms with a recently elevated conditional downside beta and weak cash coverage, high debt, or weak operating cash flow are more likely to be sold by volatility-targeting, credit-sensitive, and benchmark-constrained investors; short this wedge and buy financially buffered low-semibeta names. The premise fails if financing quality does not differentiate the forward performance of high-semibeta stocks during broad downside regimes.

factors.name: Close Auction Inventory Transfer Residual
factors.description: Approximate early-bar movement with open-to-midpoint price change and late-bar movement with midpoint-to-close change, where midpoint is derived from high and low. Compare the late directional residual with abnormal volume, close location, and the day's range to classify each move as likely inventory transfer or information-confirmed pressure, then rank the signed expected six-day response.
factors.trading_idea: When late-session price movement is unusually large relative to the day's earlier move and is accompanied by abnormal volume, the close may reflect benchmark-related inventory transfer rather than fully informative repricing. The sign of the residual is expected to mean-revert when the closing move conflicts with the broader intraday path, but to persist when it is confirmed by broad daily participation and a close near the extreme. This is a falsifiable auction-liquidity hypothesis: conditional post-close returns should differ sharply between inventory-transfer and information-confirmed states.

factors.name: Impact Surface Curvature
factors.description: Within each name, fit a causal rolling robust relationship between absolute intrabar range and relative volume across several volume quantiles. Measure the excess slope in the upper-volume tail versus the normal-volume slope, then multiply that curvature by the current signed close-location and relative-volume shock.
factors.trading_idea: Order-book depth is not constant: once the best levels are depleted, the marginal price response to an additional unit of volume rises nonlinearly. A name whose high-volume bars have recently become disproportionately range-expansive is likely experiencing latent depth depletion, so contemporaneous directional flow should have greater continuation than ordinary flow. Liquidity providers are the natural opposite side, replenishing too cautiously after abnormal consumption; the effect should disappear if estimated impact curvature does not forecast subsequent same-sign returns.

factors.name: Capacity-Adjusted Hidden Flow Release
factors.description: Estimate a rolling signed-flow imbalance using return sign times relative dollar volume, divide it by realized cumulative absolute return and a capacity proxy based on market capitalization and normal dollar volume, and require prior price compression followed by a directional envelope break. Rank the signed release score cross-sectionally, suppressing names with stale or missing capacity data.
factors.trading_idea: A sequence of high signed volume with muted cumulative price movement can represent hidden liquidity temporarily absorbing a parent order rather than the absence of information. When the latest bar finally closes outside the compressed multi-day price envelope, the accumulated flow is more likely to be released into a directional move; scaling by market capitalization and normal dollar-volume capacity separates meaningful imbalance from ordinary noise in small names. The other side is liquidity providers replenishing until their inventory tolerance is reached, and the effect should disappear if pre-break signed-flow imbalance has no relationship to post-break returns after conditioning on volume and range.

factors.name: Opening Auction Rejection Proxy
factors.description: Normalize the overnight/opening gap by trailing true range, multiply its opposite-signed intrabar rejection by abnormal volume, and cross-sectionally rank the result. A large positive score corresponds to a downward gap that is strongly rejected upward, or an upward gap that is strongly rejected downward.
factors.trading_idea: Large opening dislocations accompanied by unusually high volume but a close that travels back through the opening price indicate that one-sided opening liquidity was consumed and then replenished by passive counterparties. The likely sellers or buyers on the other side are auction participants, market makers, and value-sensitive liquidity providers responding after the opening imbalance is revealed. The signal should fail if such rejected opening gaps do not subsequently mean-revert more than comparable gaps with weak rejection, implying that the gap was information-driven rather than a temporary liquidity shock.

factors.name: Sector Participation Impact Residual
factors.description: Compute each stock's signed close-to-open move scaled by intraday range and relative volume, then subtract the analogous leave-one-out sector aggregate. Take the contrarian side of large idiosyncratic impact residuals, especially when sector participation is low.
factors.trading_idea: A stock whose signed price displacement is unusually large relative to both its own volume and contemporaneous sector participation is likely experiencing temporary inventory transfer rather than broad information incorporation. Dealers and short-horizon liquidity providers may warehouse the imbalance when sector peers do not confirm it, creating a predictable partial unwind as liquidity normalizes. The signal should fail when the same move is broadly confirmed by sector-level volume and return participation, which would indicate genuine common information rather than isolated flow.

factors.name: Volume-Clock Autocovariance Dislocation
factors.description: Construct a rolling volume clock from each stock's volume divided by its trailing average volume, scale daily log returns by that clock increment, and estimate short-lag autocovariance of the resulting volume-time return process. Cross-sectionally favor names with persistent signed volume-time displacement, while downweighting names with sparse or unstable volume histories.
factors.trading_idea: Institutional execution is typically scheduled in participation-of-volume time rather than calendar time. A stock whose signed returns remain positively autocorrelated after being normalized by its own realized volume clock is more likely to be carrying an unfinished execution program, whereas identical calendar-time moves without volume-clock persistence are more likely noise. The signal should fail if volume-normalized return persistence has no incremental forecasting power over ordinary return autocorrelation or if its effect reverses after controlling for contemporaneous liquidity.
